workflows.name: verify receipt of a native 420 transfer
workflows.objective: Confirm that a native 420 value transfer was included, executed successfully, and reached the expected destination on the expected chain.
prerequisites: qualified 420Indexer data for the target network
user_path: compare from/to/valueWei with the expected transfer
workflows.expected_result: Transaction view shows the indexed sender, recipient, native value, successful receipt status, containing block and finality.
limitations: No live deployment or representative transfer has been qualified in EXP-0.2.2.
Explorer is a projection and does not become settlement authority.
The transaction presentation currently does not expose fee calculation.
required_tests: UI transaction lookup and native-value rendering test
testnet witness comparing displayed transfer with authoritative chain data

workflows.name: confirm success or failure of a transaction
workflows.objective: Determine whether an indexed transaction executed successfully or reverted and whether its containing block is head, safe or finalized.
workflows.expected_result: Receipt status 1 is presented as SUCCESS, status 0 as REVERTED, with indexed block finality.
limitations: Pending transactions are not represented by the current indexed transaction model.
Runtime correctness against the target network remains unverified.

workflows.name: inspect transaction fees
workflows.objective: Determine the gas consumed and actual transaction fee paid.
prerequisites: effective gas price or equivalent fee inputs
workflows.expected_result: User can distinguish gas used from the actual native fee and verify the fee calculation.
limitations: Current ReceiptSummary exposes gasUsed only.
Transaction/receipt models inspected for this milestone do not expose gasPrice, effectiveGasPrice or a computed fee.
The current UI therefore cannot satisfy the full fee-inspection workflow.

workflows.name: review wallet activity
workflows.objective: Review public transaction activity associated with a wallet address.
user_path: review inbound/outbound transaction history, counterparties and value
follow transactions or blocks for detail
workflows.expected_result: Address page lists indexed transaction history with direction, counterparty, native value and snapshot/finality metadata.
limitations: Current address view is transaction-history oriented; it does not establish wallet balances or token holdings.
Viewing an address confers no wallet/private-key authority.
Runtime accuracy remains unverified.

workflows.name: locate and examine a smart contract
workflows.objective: Locate a deployed contract and inspect its indexed deployment and runtime-code facts.
prerequisites: contract address or a Registry/deployment link that resolves to it
user_path: navigate to a contract link or direct contract route
inspect deployment transaction/block, code hash and runtime bytecode
workflows.expected_result: Contract detail presents indexed deployment provenance, runtime code, code hash and chain ID.
limitations: Global search treats every 20-byte value as an address route and does not identify contract type before navigation.
No verified-source/ABI verdict is produced by Explorer itself.
Live contract data remains unverified.
required_tests: search/type-resolution acceptance test if global contract search is required

workflows.name: verify a contract deployment
workflows.objective: Correlate a deployed contract address with its creation transaction, block provenance and indexed runtime code.
prerequisites: indexed deployment transaction and contract record
user_path: confirm receipt created-contract address and successful status
workflows.expected_result: Contract and transaction views provide mutually traceable deployment provenance and runtime code facts.
limitations: This does not by itself prove source verification, compiler provenance or Registry publication.
Live deployment evidence remains a later qualification gate.

workflows.name: track token transfers
workflows.objective: Review indexed token/asset transfer activity and follow each transfer to its transaction and participants.
workflows.expected_result: Asset activity lists indexed transfers with asset identity, amount, participants and transaction provenance.
limitations: Current web page requests recent transfers without exposing assetKey/address filters even though the API accepts them.
Supported token-standard coverage and live decoder correctness remain unqualified.

workflows.name: inspect validator-produced blocks
workflows.objective: Identify which validator/proposer produced a specific block and inspect that block.
prerequisites: block producer/proposer identity attached to block provenance or a reliable block-to-consensus mapping
user_path: follow producer/validator detail or consensus context
workflows.expected_result: A block can be traced to the validator/proposer responsible for producing it.
limitations: Current BlockRecord has no proposer/validator field.
Consensus view exposes scheduled proposer information but the inspected Explorer source does not bind a historical block to a producer.
The workflow cannot currently be claimed implemented.

workflows.name: investigate a failed contract interaction
workflows.objective: Inspect a reverted contract transaction, its call input, receipt status, block/finality and emitted logs.
user_path: inspect destination, input, gas used, finality and any logs
workflows.expected_result: User can establish that the call reverted and inspect the raw indexed context around the failure.
limitations: No revert reason or decoded function call is exposed by the inspected Explorer presentation model.
No ABI-aware diagnostic explanation is currently established.

workflows.name: confirm an ecosystem application transaction
workflows.objective: Determine that a transaction interacted with an implementation published for a 420 ecosystem service and inspect the transaction outcome.
workflows.expected_result: User can correlate a generic transaction with a Registry-published service implementation without Explorer claiming application-specific execution semantics.
limitations: No application-specific transaction decoder is established by the current Explorer view.
Live Registry publication and ecosystem end-to-end witnesses remain unqualified.
Governance remains a separate unresolved scope decision from EXP-0.2.1.

workflows.name: verify an on-chain payment
workflows.objective: Verify publicly visible transfer facts for a transaction asserted by another application to represent an on-chain payment.
prerequisites: payment transaction hash and expected payer/payee/value or asset facts
user_path: open transaction and/or asset transfer record
cross-check application-specific payment semantics outside Explorer where required
workflows.expected_result: Explorer confirms the generic on-chain transfer and execution facts that are publicly indexed.
limitations: Explorer does not infer that a generic transfer satisfies an application-specific invoice, escrow or settlement rule.
Payment-protocol semantics require the owning application/protocol and later ecosystem integration evidence.
required_tests: token payment transfer witness where applicable

workflows.name: review publicly available staking or reward activity
workflows.objective: Inspect public staking lifecycle or reward activity associated with validators/accounts.
prerequisites: indexed staking/reward records or clearly identifiable protocol events
user_path: open staking/reward activity view or relevant validator/address history
workflows.expected_result: User can distinguish staking state/reward activity from generic transfers and trace it to protocol provenance.
limitations: Current Explorer API and web routes inspected for EXP-0.2.2 contain no staking/reward-specific view.
Consensus status is not a staking/reward history.
Generic address or asset history is insufficient to claim the requested workflow.

workflows.name: examine contract events
workflows.objective: Inspect logs emitted by a transaction or block and trace them to emitting addresses and transaction provenance.
user_path: inspect full event payload when later presentation supports it
workflows.expected_result: User can identify the log index, emitting address, transaction and existence/number of topics for indexed logs.
limitations: Current web table shows topic count rather than topic values and does not render log data.
No ABI-decoded event name/arguments are established in the inspected Explorer UI.

workflows.name: confirm an application's published contract address
workflows.objective: Use the Registry projection to identify an active/historical service implementation and inspect its contract record.
user_path: inspect active/latest versions and implementation address
compare code hash and activation provenance
workflows.expected_result: Registry view exposes versioned published implementation addresses and links them to contract detail.
limitations: Indexer/Explorer projection is not Registry authority.
Live Registry address, event ingestion and deployment publication remain later qualification requirements.

workflows.name: use Explorer data during troubleshooting or development
workflows.objective: Use status, block, transaction, address, contract, Registry, asset and consensus views to diagnose public chain/application activity.
prerequisites: known chain identifiers/resources or search input
user_path: check Explorer status for wrong-chain/stale/degraded conditions
workflows.expected_result: Developer can obtain read-only indexed diagnostics while seeing chain/finality/freshness provenance and explicit service failures.
limitations: Current global search recognizes only decimal block numbers, 32-byte transaction hashes and 20-byte addresses.
API documentation and live deployment/reliability qualification are later milestones.
Explorer data remains non-canonical projection data.
